messages.content: "287 :     public Map<String, Integer> getHeaderMap() {\n288 :         return new LinkedHashMap<String, Integer>(this.headerMap);\n289 :     }"

The test `testNoHeaderMap` in the `CSVParserTest` class is testing the `getHeaderMap` method of the `CSVParser` class. The test sets up a `CSVParser` instance by parsing a CSV string "a,b,c\n1,2,3\nx,y,z" using the default CSV format. Then it asserts that the `headerMap` of the parser is `null`.

Looking at the code snippet for the `parse` method, we see that it simply creates a new `CSVParser` object from the provided CSV string and the given `CSVFormat` object. The `headerMap` is not explicitly set during the parsing.

The `getHeaderMap` method of the `CSVParser` class returns a copy of the `headerMap` stored in the parser.

Therefore, in this test case, since the CSV string does not contain a header row (no explicit header), the `headerMap` should indeed be `null`. The failure of the test indicates that the `getHeaderMap` method is not returning `null` when the parser does not have a header row. This discrepancy could be due to either the parser incorrectly setting a default header map even when there is no header row or the `getHeaderMap` method not handling the absence of a header row correctly. 

Further investigation is required to pinpoint the exact cause of the failure.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
